title: Append a Bazaar string version
summary: Append complete opaque text under one ID, preserving every older version. The first update creates version one; every later update creates another version.

consumers.statement: Local programs use the in-process bazaar::api Rust API. People and authorized agents use the Bazaar CLI.

preconditions.statement: The selected database is initialized and uses Bazaar schema one. Its path is absolute, with a private regular parent directory and a private regular database file.

data_semantics.statement: Raw string operations preserve opaque UTF-8 without parsing, normalization, templating, merging, or execution. Empty content is valid. IDs are nonempty exact strings with caller-owned meaning. The separate bazaar.prompts.prepare feature owns prompt text preparation.

identity_and_units.statement: An ID and its positive integer version identify one immutable record. Versions start at one independently for each ID. There are no timestamps or measurement units.

access.statement: The current user's filesystem permissions protect state. Writer::open requires initialized private state and creates no files. Direct API appends record no CLI usage; CLI dispatch separately attempts metadata-only Chancery usage recording.

operational_limits.statement: SQLite waits up to five seconds for lock contention. Content and complete version lists are held in memory. There is no service-level latency, content-size, or throughput guarantee. A connection is not shared concurrently between threads; callers can open independent handles.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Database schema one, CLI output schema one, API types, provider release, and capability versions have separate identities. Unsupported or foreign databases fail without migration.

reliances.statement: Core string operations use local SQLite and files only. No external service, model, or installed catalog is a runtime dependency.

inputs.statement: One nonempty exact, case-sensitive ID and one complete UTF-8 content string. The CLI accepts exactly one of a positional string, --file, or --stdin. Empty strings are valid; files and stdin must decode as UTF-8.

outputs.statement: The committed Record contains id, newly allocated version, and exact content. The default CLI receipt reports the committed ID and version. Global --json wraps the complete record in existing schema-one JSON; the in-process Writer returns Record or a typed error. Record has id: String, version: i64, and content: String; bazaar::api::Result<T> uses the public typed Error. CLI operational errors exit 1: text on stderr by default, or schema-one ok:false with error.detail on stdout with --json. Syntax errors use a stderr diagnostic and exit 2 in both modes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: An update receipt describes its one committed record. It does not assert that it remains the latest after another writer appends. No recording timestamp is stored.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Each update allocates the next per-ID version and inserts the full string in one immediate SQLite transaction with synchronous FULL. Concurrent writers serialize. Identical content appends another version. SQL triggers reject updates, deletes, replacement, and nonsequential inserts. Separate update calls have no shared transaction.

use_when: The user or authorized application supplies complete new content for one ID.
Reverting a value by appending the exact contents of an older version.
do_not_use_when: The caller wants a partial patch, template expansion, content validation, deletion, or overwrite of an old version.
outcome: One new immutable version containing the supplied exact string.
effects: Appends one version to the selected initialized database. Every successful invocation appends, including repeated identical input.
authority: The caller chooses the ID and content. Bazaar owns atomic version allocation and storage, not prompt semantics or configuration validity.
success: The transaction commits and returns its exact record.
failure_and_recovery: There is no idempotency key or automatic retry. After an uncertain update, inspect history and content before deciding whether to append again. Failures do not overwrite old versions. A rollback is another explicit append.
privacy: Content is private local state and is returned in the update receipt. Prefer --file or --stdin for sensitive or multiline content rather than command arguments.
does_not_authorize: Agent execution, caller migration, model selection, interpretation of the content, removal of history, or an external send.
